name: ID-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -13 partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Simpson seeking re-election with a large financial edge
Gilbreath's fundraising is minimal, with no outside spending or polling
Prediction markets price Simpson around 95% to win
model.rationale: The district's -13 lean, Simpson's incumbency, and his roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage over Gilbreath all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets price the race near 95% Republican. With no polling or expert ratings to the contrary, the forecast stays close to fundamentals, shading slightly toward Safe R.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic spending or a polling surprise showing the race inside single digits would warrant a downgrade to Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Eastern Idaho's second district is firmly Republican territory, and veteran incumbent Mike Simpson is seeking another term with the advantages of seniority and a well-funded campaign. He has raised over $1.1 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democratic challenger Ellie Gilbreath has raised only about $107,000 and has no outside spending behind her. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but are running minimal campaigns with little money.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Republican lean, Simpson's incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture. Prediction markets give Simpson roughly a 95% chance of winning. Barring an unexpected shift, this seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands.
